version.changelog: Add native Brave API Search plugin successor link; preserve existing skill tools.

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Brave Search API integration that sends user queries to Brave and uses Brave API keys, with no evidence of hidden persistence, privilege escalation, destructive behavior, or unrelated data access.

dimensions.detail: Reading Brave API keys from environment variables and sending queries to api.search.brave.com is proportionate for this purpose; users should understand that queries and optional location/search parameters leave the local environment.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill consists of local Node.js scripts and a skill manifest; it declares no package installation, remote code loading, or system modification steps.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions clearly describe external Brave API use and required API keys, but there is a documentation inconsistency about whether non-streaming answers preserve citations and entity data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistent service, scheduled task, file mutation, root access, credential-store scraping, or system configuration change was found; caching is in-memory only.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is web search, autosuggest, spellcheck, and AI-grounded answers; the inspected scripts implement those Brave API functions and route requests to Brave endpoints.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending search terms, questions, and optional search context to Brave's API under your Brave account. Keep API keys in environment variables or an uncommitted .env file, avoid submitting secrets or sensitive personal data as queries, and monitor Brave API quota/costs. Expect Brave Answers to use English internally, and treat the non-streaming citation/entity behavior as ambiguously documented.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: scanner sub-findings looked at individual files in isolation, but the full artifact includes scripts for search, autosuggest, spellcheck, and answers, matching the combined skill purpose.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded: the .env reference is setup guidance for storing Brave API keys and the code reads specific environment variables; it does not read credential files.
[LP3] expected: Accepted only as a caution: the skill needs network and environment-variable access, but this is disclosed and scoped in practice to Brave API use.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as a documentation quality issue: the markdown gives conflicting statements about non-streaming citation and entity support, but this does not indicate malicious behavior.
[PE2] unexpected: Overridden: the cited text says the skill does not request persistent or system privileges and does not modify system config; no sudo or root command was found.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Accepted as a limitation: Brave Answers hard-codes language to English, which may surprise non-English users, but it is not a security concern.
[SQP-2] expected: Downgraded: sending the query to Brave is the core function of the answers tool and the documentation identifies Brave API use.
[SDI-1] expected: Overridden: spellcheck is explicitly listed in the README body and skill.json description, so it is not an undeclared capability.
[E1] expected: Downgraded: external transmission to api.search.brave.com is necessary for the declared Brave Search API integration and is disclosed.
[AIG] expected: The supplied A.I.G SARIF report contains no results.
